body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 9 models with a format search (of 280 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.3 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 7.4 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 6 of 8 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 43%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 67%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), layernorm bias in BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.6 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB), groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB) and layernorm output in BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.2 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): div outputs end furthest from full precision, microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition keeping only -inf dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 0.4 dB), bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 1.3 dB), linear in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 1.6 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e3m4, 7.4 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB) and silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e3m4, 9.3 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 2973 (47%), fp8_e3m4 2491 (40%), fp8_e1m6 775 (12%), ufp8_e2m6 27 (0.43%), ufp8_e3m5 1 (0.02%); 0.45% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: mul in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 38.6 dB), linear in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB) and linear in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB).

1 missing capability keep 29 operations in 3 models (of 7 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (29 operations in 3 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 29 operations in 3 models: 29 calls (1.10% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in openai-community/gpt2 and embedding in BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5. Cost today: 0 of 29 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 1 failed and 28 wait for one; 60 workarounds proposed, 7 passing its check, 12 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 457 of 774 tensors passed between kernels (59%) in 7 models: 291 for attention heads split or merged, 146 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 291 operations (291 calls, 11% of all calls; 101 G MACs, 4.21% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 84 and linear → add (other reshapes) 62; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (200), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and google/vit-base-patch16-224 (36).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 457 of 774 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 772 operations in 7 models (772 calls, 29% of all calls), most often silu (210), layernorm (185) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst 9.2 dB SQNR over 772 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 22, most 82 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 82 planned groups), over 7 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

1 accuracy run produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 1 kernel measured.
title: Resource limits: 772 operations limited by the LUT and up to 82 kernel launches per pass

body:
**IPU cost summary (most costly first):**

1. **Layout conversions are the most widespread cost:** 457 of 774 tensors (59%) passed between kernels must be rearranged by the reading kernel, holding 101 G MACs (4.21% of all MACs) across 291 operations, mostly from attention head splits/merges after linear layers. 2. **Resource limits affect the most operations:** 772 operations (29% of calls) rely on a 256-entry LUT for activations like silu and layernorm, limiting quantized accuracy to a worst case of 9.2 dB SQNR, plus up to 82 kernel launches per pass. 3. **Format precision losses are significant but model-dependent:** NX8 formats lose up to 12.8 dB SQNR (median 23.3 dB) on model outputs, with 5 of 7 models degrading on prediction metrics (e.g., token agreement dropping from 100% to 66%). 4. **Missing run-time addressing blocks 29 operations** (embedding lookups) in 3 models from running directly, though these carry no MACs and have no working workaround yet (28 still waiting). 5. **Binary compute is entirely stalled:** MAC utilisation is 0% across all 14 measured cases, meaning the multipliers cannot be kept fed at all.
